fortisbc-custom-efficiency-study.name: Custom Efficiency Program - energy study funding
fortisbc-custom-efficiency-study.summary: Up to 50% of an energy study by a FortisBC-approved consultant (max $20,000 for commercial buildings), plus an implementation bonus of up to another 50% of the study cost (max $20,000) once approved measures are installed. Implementation incentives: the lesser of $6/GJ (gas) or $0.03/kWh (electric) over measure life, 75% of invoiced costs, or $500,000 for commercial buildings.
fortisbc-custom-efficiency-study.eligibility: FortisBC natural gas customers on any rate class except Rate 1 and/or FortisBC or listed municipal electricity customers; existing commercial, institutional or multi-unit residential buildings (also industrial/agricultural); project must be able to save 1,000 GJ gas or 50,000 kWh per year; written approval before the study starts.

fortisbc-rental-apartment-efficiency.name: Energy efficiency for rental apartments and accommodations program
fortisbc-rental-apartment-efficiency.summary: Free building energy assessment by FortisBC engineering consultants plus free in-suite showerheads, aerators, pipe insulation and hot-water recirculation controls, with ongoing support for larger upgrades.
fortisbc-rental-apartment-efficiency.eligibility: Purpose-built rentals: apartment buildings, hotels/motels and private retirement or care homes with 9+ units, on a commercial rate for FortisBC gas and/or electricity (or listed municipal utilities), with central gas water heating (central electric water heating only for FortisBC/municipal electric customers; BC Hydro customers with central electric water heating are not eligible).

fortisbc-small-business-support.name: Energy-saving support for small businesses program
fortisbc-small-business-support.summary: Free customized energy advice (15-30 minute consultation by phone, video or in person), which may include a basic energy assessment and rebate information, with a follow-up email.
fortisbc-small-business-support.eligibility: Small and medium-sized businesses; GreenStep makes outbound visits in listed communities: Burnaby, Tri-Cities, North Vancouver, Surrey, Richmond, Maple Ridge, West Vancouver, Vancouver (downtown), Langley, Abbotsford, Kelowna, West Kelowna, Winfield, Penticton, Summerland, Oliver, Nanaimo, Courtenay ('Courtney' on the page), Campbell River, Coombs, Parksville, Port Alberni.
fortisbc-small-business-support.note: A short consultation, not a full audit.

cleanbc-custom-programs.name: CleanBC Custom and Custom-Lite programs
cleanbc-custom-programs.summary: Past funding for energy studies (Custom: up to $20,000; Custom-Lite: up to $2,000) and upgrades in commercial, industrial and multi-unit residential buildings.

ab-ceip-commercial.name: Clean Energy Improvement Program (CEIP) - commercial
ab-ceip-commercial.summary: Property-assessed financing (not a grant) of up to 100% of eligible energy-efficiency and renewable upgrade costs, repaid through the property tax bill (terms up to 20 years for some upgrades). Pre-qualification requires an ASHRAE Level 2 audit report, or a quote showing one is booked (plus a feasibility study for non-solar renewables); a post-project memo from an energy-audit engineering consultant is also required.
ab-ceip-commercial.eligibility: Commercial properties in municipalities with a commercial program: City of Calgary, Sturgeon County and City of Edmonton (Grande Prairie listed as launching soon).
ab-ceip-commercial.note: The pages don't say the audit cost itself can be financed. Included because the program requires an audit.

mccac-cec.name: Community Energy Conservation (CEC) program
mccac-cec.summary: Paid municipalities up to 50% of pre-GST energy audit costs per facility (max $7,500) plus retrofit rebates, for municipally owned facilities.

era-energy-savings-for-business.name: Energy Savings for Business (ESB)
era-energy-savings-for-business.summary: Past commercial energy-efficiency incentive program (CES, ESB, ETP and SPEED streams).
era-energy-savings-for-business.note: ERA: 'all current funding ... has been awarded.'

energy-efficiency-alberta.name: Energy Efficiency Alberta (agency)
energy-efficiency-alberta.summary: Former provincial energy-efficiency agency and program provider.
energy-efficiency-alberta.note: Closure (2020) is from the task brief; no official closure notice was found in this pass. The efficiencyalberta.ca domain did not respond on 2026-09-28, and alberta.ca has only an archived 2016 engagement page.

saskpower-ceop.name: Commercial Energy Optimization Program (CEOP)
saskpower-ceop.provider: SaskPower and SaskEnergy (administered by CLEAResult, with the Government of Canada)
saskpower-ceop.summary: Free consulting. Energy Support Services (small/medium businesses using under 2 GWh/yr): identify opportunities, build business cases, track projects and savings. Energy Coach Services (large, about 2 GWh+): the same plus up to $30,000 toward an energy champion. CEOP Incentive Services for upgrades: $0.13/kWh non-lighting, $0.06/kWh lighting, $15/GJ gas, up to 50% of costs and $100,000 per project per fuel.
saskpower-ceop.eligibility: Commercial customers connected to the SaskPower-controlled grid; facilities mainly used for manufacturing, processing or raw-material extraction are not eligible.
saskpower-ceop.note: Only Energy Support Services is still taking participants, and it 'has limited availability and may close at any time without notice.' Energy Coach Services closed to new enrolment April 30, 2026. The Incentive Services pre-application deadline was July 31, 2026 (case-by-case exceptions for projects finished by Dec 31, 2026).

efficiencymb-commercial-energy-audit.name: Commercial Energy Audit Program
efficiencymb-commercial-energy-audit.summary: Up to 50% of the cost of an ASHRAE Level 2 or Level 3 audit by a pre-qualified consultant. Caps (L2 / L3): office, education, hotel, recreation/arena, healthcare, multi-unit residential or industrial-with-offices buildings of 4+ storeys (any size) or 1-3 storeys over 60,000 sq ft: $3,200 / $12,500; 1-3 storeys 30,000-60,000 sq ft: $2,200 / $8,000; 1-3 storeys under 30,000 sq ft, and all other building types: $1,200 / $4,200.
efficiencymb-commercial-energy-audit.eligibility: Commercial buildings whose owner is a Manitoba Hydro customer on a commercial rate, heated mainly by electricity or natural gas supplied by Manitoba Hydro; pre-qualified auditor; approval before any site work; audit done within 6 months.

efficiencymb-small-business.name: Small Business Program
efficiencymb-small-business.summary: Free installation of basic energy-saving products plus a free lighting and pitched-roof attic insulation assessment to see if a Premium Upgrade fits.
efficiencymb-small-business.eligibility: Small business owners (details on program sub-pages, not read).

ens-small-business-assessment.name: Free energy assessments for small businesses (Small Business Energy Solutions)
ens-small-business-assessment.summary: Free energy assessment (in person or by phone) with a custom report on the best upgrades and available rebates.
ens-small-business-assessment.eligibility: Businesses with electricity costs under $6,000/month, whatever the heating fuel; capacity is limited and applying doesn't guarantee an assessment.
ens-small-business-assessment.note: The SBES rebate budget for 2026 is fully committed: new pre-approvals are still issued, but their rebates will be paid in 2027.

ens-custom-retrofit-study.name: Building Energy Retrofits (Custom Retrofit) - scoping and feasibility study incentives
ens-custom-retrofit-study.summary: Scoping study rebate: 50% of cost up to $1,000 (P.Eng-signed). Feasibility study incentive: up to $15,000 (up to 100% of study cost) with pre-approval, paid at 100% if the project goes ahead to a Custom Project Agreement and 50% if it doesn't. Implementation incentive: the larger of $0.15/kWh or $250/kW of peak demand savings, limited to 50% of incremental costs and $750,000 per project, minus any study incentives.
ens-custom-retrofit-study.eligibility: Non-residential customers or farm operations; institutional, non-profit, commercial (including multi-unit residential) or industrial facilities served directly or indirectly by Nova Scotia Power and using at least 350,000 kWh/yr; projects must save at least 15,000 kWh/yr. Electricity-reduction projects only.
ens-custom-retrofit-study.note: Amounts come from the guidelines PDF linked on the live page (file named 2025; document dated November 2023).

ens-building-optimization.name: Building Optimization Program (recommissioning)
ens-building-optimization.summary: Funding covers 100% of an Investigation Study, up to $5,000, to assess building systems and recommend operational (recommissioning) improvements.
ens-building-optimization.eligibility: Commercial, industrial and institutional buildings in Nova Scotia; work with a contractor from ENS's qualified network.

nbpower-cbrp-audit.name: Commercial Buildings Retrofit Program - energy audit and feasibility study incentives
nbpower-cbrp-audit.summary: ASHRAE Level II audit: 50% of cost up front, max $1,100 (under 15,000 sq ft), $2,200 (15,000-75,000 sq ft) or $3,300 (over 75,000 sq ft); rises to 100% of audit cost, max $3,000 / $5,000 / $8,000 (including the first payment), once one or more recommended measures are done. Feasibility study (instead of a full audit): 100% of cost up to $1,100 / $2,200 / $3,300 when the measure is implemented. Upgrade incentives: $120/GJ for electricity-saving projects (up to $250,000 per fiscal year) and 25% for non-electric upgrades (capped at $1 million per entity).
nbpower-cbrp-audit.eligibility: Commercial or institutional buildings on NB Power General Service 1 or 2 rates; non-NB Power customers in a similar rate class are also eligible; also registered farms, places of worship and multi-unit residential buildings with 3+ units. Work goes through an approved Energy Management Service Provider (EMSP).
nbpower-cbrp-audit.note: Program guide v71, June 2026. Non-electric upgrade funds are first come, first served until depleted.

nbpower-energy-walkthrough.name: Free Energy Walk-Through Service
nbpower-energy-walkthrough.summary: Free site visit by a Technical Energy Advisor to find energy-saving projects and matching rebates.
nbpower-energy-walkthrough.eligibility: All businesses in New Brunswick, whatever their energy provider or fuel.

efficiencypei-strategic-energy-solutions.name: Strategic Energy Solutions for Business, Commercial and Community Buildings
efficiencypei-strategic-energy-solutions.summary: efficiencyPEI connects applicants with an auditor for a free ASHRAE Level 1 commercial energy audit. Feasibility study funding by annual energy use: $0 (0-100,000 ekWh), $5,000 (100,000-250,000), $10,000 (250,000-500,000), $15,000 (500,000+ ekWh). Upgrade incentive: the lowest of 1x annual savings, 50% of project cost or $75,000 (annual rebate caps $25,000 / $35,000 / $50,000 / $75,000 by tier).
efficiencypei-strategic-energy-solutions.eligibility: Buildings owned and operated by businesses, institutions, municipalities or non-profits; apply with 12 months of utility bills.
efficiencypei-strategic-energy-solutions.note: Current incentive levels in effect since June 2, 2025.

takecharge-business-efficiency.name: Business Efficiency Program - Custom Solutions
takecharge-business-efficiency.provider: takeCHARGE (Newfoundland Power and Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro)
takecharge-business-efficiency.summary: Step 1 is a high-level energy assessment by a TakeCharge energy expert, 'fully funded by TakeCharge'; where a detailed energy audit or feasibility study is needed, 'TakeCharge funding may also be available' (no amount stated). Upgrade incentive: $0.10/kWh of first-year savings, max $100,000, plus a limited-time bonus of $500 per kW of peak demand reduced (offer until Dec 31, 2026; measures in service by Dec 31, 2027).
takecharge-business-efficiency.eligibility: Commercial customers (details via TakeCharge; M&V required at close-out).

yukon-commercial-rebates.name: Rebates for energy upgrades to commercial and institutional buildings
yukon-commercial-rebates.summary: Rebates for energy upgrades (small projects: heat pumps, ENERGY STAR appliances/windows, biomass, HRVs, insulation/air sealing, solar hot water). Large projects need an energy model by an engineer or certified technician showing at least 20% carbon reduction; funding up to 25% for for-profits (40% for biomass/heat pumps in existing buildings), 50% for non-profits, 60% for First Nations, municipalities and Crown corporations. No standalone rebate for audits or energy models was found.
yukon-commercial-rebates.eligibility: First Nations governments and development corporations, municipalities, non-profits/NGOs, for-profit businesses, Crown corporations, and owners of multi-unit residential buildings over 600 m2.
yukon-commercial-rebates.note: Not an audit incentive. Listed so Whitehorse pages can say what exists. The page was last updated June 2025, with no 2026 closure notice.

aea-building-energy-audits.name: Building Improvements - building energy audits
aea-building-energy-audits.summary: Free desktop 'yardstick' audits (utility bill analysis) and free on-site targeted audits (heating, ventilation, air leakage, water equipment, lighting) for businesses and non-profits; community governments pay a fee but may get a $15,000 subsidy. Upgrade rebates up to $50,000 (up to $75,000 for community and Indigenous governments and Indigenous development corporations), the lower of 50% of eligible costs or a savings-based calculation.
aea-building-energy-audits.eligibility: Businesses, non-profits and community governments in the NWT. No rebates for systems that burn fossil fuels.

fcm-gmf-green-buildings-pathway-study.name: Green Municipal Fund - Feasibility study: Green Buildings Pathway
fcm-gmf-green-buildings-pathway-study.provider: Federation of Canadian Municipalities (Green Municipal Fund)
fcm-gmf-green-buildings-pathway-study.summary: Grant for up to 80% of eligible costs, max $65,000 for one building or $200,000 for a portfolio, to plan GHG-reduction upgrades.
fcm-gmf-green-buildings-pathway-study.eligibility: Municipal governments, their project partners and not-for-profits that own community buildings (ice rinks, arenas, pools, community/recreation centres, arts and culture facilities, libraries, multi-purpose buildings). Not for private commercial buildings.
fcm-gmf-green-buildings-pathway-study.note: Accepts applications year-round until funding runs out. National, so it is kept out of cityIncentives (see nationalIncentives).

Toronto Hydro.usageDownload: Log in to My Account (self-serve portal), then Green Button Download My Data: consumption, billing and customer info as Green Button XML. Register online if you have no account.

Hydro Ottawa.usageDownload: MyAccount: view and download up to 24 months of hourly usage as Excel, PDF or Green Button (XML).

Hydro One.usageDownload: myAccount, then Green Button Download My Data: up to 24 months of billing, consumption and transaction data (XML).

Alectra Utilities.usageDownload: My Alectra account, then Green Button: download or connect electricity usage, billing and account data (XML). Interval-metered businesses also get a CSV energy-usage portal with 24 months of data.

London Hydro.usageDownload: MyLondonHydro portal, then Green Button Download My Data (XML) of historical and current usage.

Enova Power.usageDownload: My Account or the Green Button page: Download My Data in XML (you need your account number and meter number).

ENWIN Utilities.usageDownload: myENWIN portal, then 'Green Button' in the left sidebar, then Download my Data (consumption and/or billing). Live since Dec 5, 2022.

Oakville Hydro.usageDownload: MyOakvilleHydro account plus the Green Button platform: Download My Data (XML).

Burlington Hydro.usageDownload: MyBurlingtonHydro account, then Green Button Download My Data (historical and current usage in a standard format).

Oshawa Power.usageDownload: MyOshawaPower portal (billing and usage tracking). Green Button is required of every Ontario rate-regulated distributor since Nov 1, 2023 (OEB), but oshawapower.ca blocked our fetch (HTTP 403), so the exact Green Button path is unverified.

Greater Sudbury Hydro.usageDownload: MyAccount (myaccount.gsuinc.ca), then Green Button Download My Data.

Elexicon Energy.usageDownload: my.elexicon, then the Green Button logo, then Download My Data (XML). Or use the Green Button portal with a recent bill. Up to 2 years of historical usage.

GrandBridge Energy.usageDownload: Green Button Download My Data (XML) via the My Account portal or a direct link on the GrandBridge site.

Milton Hydro.usageDownload: MyAccount, then the Smart Meter tab, then Downloads, then Green Button (hourly data).

Kingston Hydro.usageDownload: Utilities Kingston Green Button portal (validate with a recent bill), then Download My Data: up to 2 years of electricity, gas, water and wastewater usage (XML). The MyUtilities account has a combined bill.

Synergy North.usageDownload: MyENERGY portal: hourly, daily and monthly usage graphs plus Green Button Download My Data / Connect My Data.

Entegrus Powerlines.usageDownload: Entegrus MyAccount, then Green Button Download My Data.

Hydro-Québec.usageDownload: Customer Space (Espace client), then My electricity use / Detailed consumption: hour-to-hour, daily, monthly and bill-to-bill history with year-over-year comparison. No Green Button offering found, and a file-export option wasn't confirmed.

Hydro-Sherbrooke.usageDownload: Mon compte Hydro portal: e-bill, balance and 'Consulter votre consommation' (view consumption). History depth and export not stated.

Hydro-Jonquière.usageDownload: Hydro-Jonquière's online billing service: view annual consumption and all account transactions. No data download or history depth is mentioned.

ENMAX Power.usageDownload: ENMAX Power (the wires company) doesn't bill homes, so usage history comes from your retailer's bills or online account, e.g. ENMAX Energy MyAccount for ENMAX retail and Rate of Last Resort customers. No distributor usage portal or Green Button found; the ENMAX MyAccount page only confirms bills and payments.

EPCOR.usageDownload: EPCOR's advanced meters send daily reads to your retailer; use your retailer's bills or portal. EPCOR Energy (RoLR) and Encor customers see bills in EPCOR MyAccount, which stores bills for up to two years. No usage download or Green Button confirmed.

FortisAlberta.usageDownload: FortisAlberta My Account (a distributor portal, separate from your retailer): up to two years of daily consumption in daily or monthly views, downloadable to Excel for a chosen date range. No Green Button mentioned.

City of Red Deer Electric Light & Power.usageDownload: No customer usage portal found. Meters are read manually monthly until the AMI rollout (residential installs from spring 2026), so use your retailer's bills or online account (default RoLR: ENMAX Energy).

City of Lethbridge Electric Utility.usageDownload: No distributor usage portal found. Usage history comes from your retailer's bills or account; the City of Lethbridge is itself the default Rate of Last Resort retailer.

SaskPower.usageDownload: MySaskPower, then My Reports: Compare Bills, Power Consumption (smart-meter power reports) and a 'Download Data' report. Smart-meter accounts also get Power Use Alerts. Export format not stated.

Saskatoon Light & Power.usageDownload: City of Saskatoon 'My Utility Account': Utility Consumption Summary and detailed consumption and charges. SmartUTIL (opened from My Utility Account) shows electricity and water use by month, day or hour.

Manitoba Hydro.usageDownload: Online account (web or app): current and past bills for up to two years plus energy-use tracking. Manitoba Hydro also supplies Winnipeg's natural gas.

BC Hydro.usageDownload: MyHydro account: hourly, daily and weekly consumption, comparisons with the same period last year and with similar homes. Export and Green Button not confirmed (the page content is script-rendered).

FortisBC.usageDownload: Account Online: review billing information and energy usage (same login for FortisBC electricity in Kelowna and FortisBC gas). Its 'My energy use' tool adds an appliance-level breakdown. Export and Green Button not confirmed.

Nova Scotia Power.usageDownload: MyAccount, then MyEnergy Insights (smart-meter customers): usage by hour, day, month and year, plus an appliance breakdown and alerts. As of Sept 2026 the page says MyEnergy Insights is still being restored after NS Power's cyber incident.

NB Power.usageDownload: Online NB Power account: Consumption History graph. Smart-meter customers see usage by day, hour or 15 minutes with temperature overlay and alerts. The site notes a systems upgrade may leave gaps or estimates in the online usage graph.

Saint John Energy.usageDownload: Not verified: the sjenergy.ca site failed TLS verification from our fetcher. Ask the utility about an online account or 12-month history.

Maritime Electric.usageDownload: MyPower account: consumption history and bill/payment history for the past five years. A new AMI customer portal with interval data is being rolled out (island-wide AMI by 2027).

Newfoundland Power.usageDownload: My Account: Usage / Energy Usage (compare with the same month last year), Billing History and a 'Download Account History' option, plus an Annual Electricity Statement.

ATCO Electric Yukon.usageDownload: My Account Portal: statements on any device and monitoring of energy consumption. History depth and download not stated.

Naka Power Utilities (formerly Northland.usageDownload: My Account Portal: statements, e-bills and energy consumption on the account. AMI smart-meter installs expected to start Q3/Q4 2026. History depth and download not stated.

Enbridge Gas.usageDownload: Gas utility (most of Ontario): My Account, then Share My Data, then Download your Data: up to 24 months of billing and usage data as Green Button XML.
